title: Nutcrackers
prompt: a pair of nutcrackers holding a walnut on a table with three buttons: “Load” seats the nut between the jaws; “Squeeze” breaks its shell; “Move nut” places it nearer the hinge to increase force; see-through reveals the paired second-class levers and shell contact points
blurb: A table-top teaching adaptation shows how paired second-class levers crack a walnut and gain force nearer the hinge.

identity.note: Levers / Second-class levers, page 20, and Nutcrackers in Levers in action, page 22. Paired second-class levers compress shell between hinge and hand effort.
identity.classificationNote: A named machine or diagram inside Levers is not a separate main chapter. The parking-meter heading is historical.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct from first-class pliers and scissors and third-class tweezers. Nail-clippers combine a second-class handle with third-class cutting blades.

prompt.note: Faithful. Load seats the nut, Squeeze cracks it, and Move nut can compare force nearer the hinge at unchanged finger effort. Reopen the jaws and supply a fresh intact shell or explicit reset before repeating. Do not silently heal a broken shell.

truthNotes.construction: Representative end-hinged metal arms with interleaved hinge eyes, pin, integral serrated jaw edges and covered hand grips. No extra powered hardware.
teachingAdaptations: The table and three specimen walnuts stage the lesson.
Load lifts a supply walnut into the opened jaws. After a crack it sets the old shell aside and loads a different nut. When the batch is exhausted Load explicitly replenishes it.
Move nut opens and reseats the same walnut nearer the hinge. It preserves shell damage.
See-through fades the arms and grips, shows the hinge pin and kernel, and overlays both lever axes, effort arrows and shell contact points. Overlays and specimens do not count as anatomy.
truthNotes.forceModel: Illustrative ideal static force for 35 N perpendicular effort on each grip at arm length 72. Load arm is (nutX - hingeX) cos(angle). Force shown is per jaw, not the sum of the opposed forces. Friction, shell fracture threshold and tissue deformation are not measured.
